title: Is your rest timer costing you strength?
voice_direction: Conversational British training partner; brisk and curious, never announcer-like. Distributed synthetic stock voice; no human impersonation.
script: Your one-minute rest timer might be costing you strength. One minute versus three: in a small eight-week trial, the three-minute group gained more squat and bench strength. Same planned workouts. Different breaks. So why rush back just to struggle through the next set? This was twenty-one trained men, so three minutes isn't a magic rule for everyone. But if your reps keep falling off a cliff, try resting longer and compare. And be honest: do you actually feel ready, or do you just feel guilty sitting still? What's your rest time? And which lift?

sources.title: Longer Interset Rest Periods Enhance Muscle Strength and Hypertrophy in Resistance-Trained Men
sources.design: Randomized trial; 21 young resistance-trained men; eight weeks; one versus three minutes between sets; three full-body sessions per week.
sources.claim_scope: The three-minute group improved squat and bench 1RM more and gained more anterior-thigh muscle thickness. Do not generalize this to every muscle or demographic.

public_citation_policy: No burned citations or paper references in public caption; evidence is retained in internal provenance.
factual_caveat: Small eight-week trial of 21 young resistance-trained men; not a universal prescription. Same planned sessions, not necessarily equal completed training volume.
revision_reason: Owner requested faster, more engaging cut without academic footers, references or draft labels.
